headline: Oilers take accountability message from coach Mike Babcock's healthy scratches
take:
Per ESPN, new Oilers coach Mike Babcock is making his approach clear early in the season through lineup decisions, with healthy scratches carrying an accountability message. Oilersnation, posting for Daily Faceoff Edmonton, adds that defenceman Jake Walman could be a healthy scratch again tomorrow.

The numbers back up why those two are under the microscope. Trent Frederic has one goal in 12 games so far this season, playing 9.59 minutes a night. At 5-on-5, EDM has just 42 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice, and the team's share is 7.9 points better without him. Walman is a similar case: 46 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals, and the team does 2.79 points better when he's off the ice. His one assist in nine games is about what his chances predict, since his own expected goals are just 0.52. EDM's 9-2-2 record looks sturdy, but the team's 49 percent 5-on-5 share is only even, and goaltending has cost them 6.4 goals against what the shots called for. If a coach wants to explain a lineup change, these are the kinds of numbers he would point to.
